findings.reason: the next node dispatched by the plan's own open chain would be sent at §3 and would either duplicate §21 or stop, leaving the local-lane measurement unbuilt while §20 routes every figure review to that lane.
findings.text: the plan's open followup `f-arcstf-007` carries the next one-line invocation as `/reckon-build a-review-can-see-the-figure §3`, but §21 is the section that performs that measurement (its Why is written from §3's evaluation and it is the only implementable section for it), while §3 is a prose design section with no `data-id` or status, so the chain points at a section that cannot be built and s21 is reachable from nothing

findings.reason: §20 makes clive the only lane a figure review may take and can be built before s21 runs, so the plan enables routing on the evidence it says is insufficient, and an `untrusted` verdict would leave live figure reviews on a lane measured as unable to judge figures with nothing to act on it.
findings.text: s21's Why says §13 measured only that clive receives an image, not that it applies one of the rules, yet §20 (and the `figure-review-on-metered-lane` rationale) rests on §13's receipt as the reason figure reviews may run only on clive, and neither an edge nor the decision makes §20's rule wait on s21's `trusted`/`partly`/`untrusted` verdict

findings.reason: a reader taking the discriminates rule literally would count every pair as failing it and write `untrusted`, which is the inverse of what the same section's control requirement ("opened no file") asks for; the fix is one clause exempting the control from the sha256 term, and one of the two readings is wrong either way.
findings.text: the rule "A pair discriminates when the bad figure's word is FAIL, the good figure's is PASS, the control's is not FAIL, and every run involved passes the Read and sha256 checks" applies a sha256 check to the control run of each pair, which has no input image, so as written the control cannot satisfy the condition that decides whether the pair counts
